counterfactual_missing_items: No current endoscopic or histologic evidence of active ulcerative colitis
No hemolysis, dactylitis, or other acute sickle vaso-occlusive findings
Direct immunofluorescence of the lesion was negative
decisive_items: a repeat skin biopsy showed subcorneal and subepidermal edema and a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa
biopsy at that time revealed a neutrophilic panniculitis
a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa
response.rationale: R3 is directly supported by two biopsy-confirmed raw spans showing neutrophilic panniculitis, while R2 and R5 rely on historical attribution and GI symptoms without current confirmatory evidence. R1 and R6 are disfavored by the absence of vasculitic histology and negative DIF. C1 is a redundant acute-modifier completion of R3.

rejected.why: Correlated restatement of R3; adds only 'acute' without independent raw support beyond the same neutrophilic infiltrate.
History of sickle cell disease and prior attribution are nonspecific; no acute vaso-occlusive or hemolytic evidence is present.
Skin lesions and joint swelling are nonspecific; biopsy shows panniculitis, not vasculitis, and DIF is negative.
Azathioprine exposure is a nonspecific drug history; no vasculitic histology or positive DIF supports drug-induced vasculitis.
No raw support; autoimmune hepatitis history alone does not explain the skin biopsy or current presentation.
